newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan says more review needed on mobile phones.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan says more review needed on mobile phones.

text.p: Taiwan's Ministry of Transport and Communications said on Friday that Saturday's hotly anticipated announcement of winners for lucrative mobile phone franchises would be only preliminary and that further review was needed.

For weeks, the ministry has said it would identify what officials referred to as the winning bidders for the island's eight mobile operation licences on January 4, giving every indication that the review was final, not preliminary.
Officials told Reuters as recently as December 28 that have the ministry was "very close" to finalising its selections in a process it had pledged to complete in 1996.

Seventeen joint ventures, some led by major international telecom firms, have submitted 42 applications to run the newly liberalised mobile telephone franchises that analysts say could yield up to US$3.6 billion a year in sales after 10 years.

The foreign and domestic applicants include AT&T, Sprint Corp, Southwestern Bell and Air Touch of the United States, Hong Kong Telecommunications, Japan's Mitsubishi as well as Acer and the influential Koo's Group of Taiwan.

The mobile telephone sector is one of several liberalised by the parliament in January 1996 when it dismantled a decades-old state telecom monopoly by opening them up for private and limited foreign investment.
